Definition: to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall
BiblicalUsage: To stumble is what weak legs do, and Scripture uses it for the righteous man who falls seven times and gets up again, for young men who faint and grow weary, and for the proud who trip over their own sin. The word covers a tottering step and a full collapse, and it falls on the wicked and the weary alike. Yet the same word carries the promise that the just shall walk in the ways of the Lord, and the transgressors shall fall in them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe stumbling is not the end of the story for God's people, because the same God who watches the fall also steadies the step. I hold that the difference is never whether we stumble but whether we get up and walk on, and that is grace, not strength of our own.
